title: iPhone Camera Shutter
blurb: There is no shutter. Phone cameras have no moving parts to click, so Apple synthesised the sound and made it mandatory in certain markets — Japan and South Korea both require an audible shutter, which is why iPhones there refuse to be silenced. The result is that a fake mechanical noise became the universal signal of being photographed, wanted or otherwise. Use it in edits for a photo moment, or play it behind somebody to convince them they have just been captured mid-embarrassment. Everyone checks. Nobody is ever quite sure.
